bsm_10.text: A hand presses to the glass from the inside. It's a very good hand. It has never held anything, yet.

bsm_11.text: Halcyon Re-You™. We take your impression now, while you're standing there breathing and signing things.

bsm_12.text: And on the day it all goes wrong out there, and it does go wrong out there, you open your eyes on our floor, whole, warm, and owed a second go at it.

bsm_13.text: Not a copy. Not a keepsake. A second chance, in your own face, with your own bad ideas still intact.

bsm_15.text: A beige couch that has never been in anybody's home. A woman sits on it with the posture of someone who has been told to relax.

bsm_17.text: I remember getting caught out in the rain without a hood, and I remember thinking, well, that was stupid. And then I remember the ceiling here.

bsm_18.text: Nothing in between. I was waiting on a tunnel and a light and a couple of dead relatives. What I got was a gap, like nodding off on a tram.

bsm_19.text: Best thing about it? I got my whole twenties back and I already know how they end.

bsm_21.text: A man in a work jacket, hands folded, both of them noticeably newer than his face.

bsm_23.text: The lads had a bet on how I'd go. Nobody had "vending machine." I came back four hours later and settled it myself, which they didn't enjoy.

bsm_24.text: Walking home with no boots and no coat, that's the humbling part. Halcyon gives you your life back. Your trousers are between you and the city.

bsm_25.message: shrugs with the calm of a man who has done this twice

bsm_27.text: A young woman, delighted, sitting far too close to the lens.

bsm_29.text: Everyone goes on about how you'd live differently if you got another go. I've had another go. I do exactly the same things, just faster.

bsm_3.text: ♪ Three chrome tones, warm and unhurried, the kind of sound a waiting room plays at you until you agree. ♪

bsm_30.text: I'm braver now! Not smarter. Nobody claimed smarter. But you try a thing, and it goes badly, and then you're up and you're trying it again by lunch.

bsm_31.text: Honestly the worst part is finding out who kept your stuff.

bsm_33.text: A very large man on a very small cushion, still faintly annoyed about something.

bsm_35.text: Freight train. Through the Yards. And before anybody says anything: in my defence, it was a very long way off when I set out.

bsm_36.text: I could see it the whole time. It could see me the whole time. We both had ample opportunity to reconsider and neither of us took it.

bsm_37.text: Halcyon had me up by teatime, and I'll be honest, the walk home was worse than the train. Train was quick. Walk was forty minutes with no trousers past everyone I know.

bsm_38.message: stares into the middle distance, reliving a specific injustice

bsm_40.text: An older woman on the same couch, alone, very composed, hands flat on her knees.

bsm_42.text: It wasn't me, it was Wallace. Thirty-one years married. He went out for a fuse and came back on the Thursday, no coat, no boots, very cheerful.

bsm_43.text: He's left-handed now. Thirty-one years right-handed, and he comes back through that door buttering toast the wrong way about like it's nothing.

bsm_44.text: He doesn't like fish. He's never not liked fish. And he's polite to me, which he wasn't, and which I've decided I'll allow.

bsm_45.text: Can't remember our wedding. Can remember every word of a song neither of us ever liked. I've stopped asking. It only upsets the one of us who was there.

bsm_46.message: adjusts her cardigan with enormous dignity

bsm_47.text: No, I shan't be putting in a complaint. I've thought about it. He does the washing up now.

bsm_50.text: A Halcyon clerk stamps a form without looking up. Behind her, the calm eye watches the skyline, and the skyline watches nothing at all.

bsm_51.text: So take the shortcut through the Yards. Say the thing to the man with the bat. Swim out a bit further than you should.

bsm_52.text: Halcyon Re-You™. Coverage begins the moment you stop, and so, thankfully, do you.
